A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaVideoRAG framework and HiVU benchmark. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, including the image-based appendix examples and prompts. Relocated sections can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on MLVU, Video-MME and HiVU, component ablations, a sampling-density study and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds classifier comparisons, fixed-routing ablations and construction, inference and parallelization timings.

M1.justification: The classifier, three retrieval paths, multimodal indexing, evidence filtering, generation equation and classification prompt are unchanged. The added classifier substitutions and parallel-execution experiments do not establish a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use HiVU, Video-MME and MLVU with the same video domains and QA coverage. The added router checks and timing measurements examine existing components on retained data; the 100-video timing subset changes the protocol rather than coverage.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. New Table 6 evaluates Qwen2.5-1.5B and VideoLLaMA3-7B as alternative classifiers against the retained Qwen2.5-7B classifier, adding limited component-level comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces classifier precision against HiVU level labels and controls forcing every query through L1, L2 or L3. Section 4.3 adds a distinct timing protocol on 100 randomly selected MLVU videos, separating construction and inference and testing single-process, dual-process and eight-GPU configurations. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 ablates graph, visual and text retrieval and varies frame density. v3 retains these analyses and adds classifier replacement, classifier removal with fixed routing, and construction/inference/scaling analyses. These substantially expand direct examination of the central adaptive-routing and efficiency mechanisms.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experiments. The new timing averages and randomly sampled video subset do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5, Table A1 and the qualitative examples retain their results. v3 adds HiVU classifier precisions of 0.41, 0.81 and 0.48; fixed L1/L2/L3 Video-MME scores of 64.2, 67.5 and 67.1 versus adaptive routing's 68.5; and extensive timing results, including single-process response times of 8/26/27 seconds by route and 20 seconds for AdaVideoRAG.

T1.justification: The intent-classification formulation and piecewise generation equation (1) are unchanged. Neither version provides theorems or proofs, and the additions introduce no new mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about adaptive retrieval, Omni-Knowledge Indexing, efficiency and accuracy, and the HiVU benchmark. The new experiments provide supporting evidence without changing those claims' scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds discussion attributing the measured L3 construction overhead to graph building and explaining savings through adaptive scheduling and parallel execution. It removes v1's specific speculation about improved results from 671B models while retaining the model-scale and three-routing-level limitations.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly documents H20 hardware, 96 GB memory, batch size 2, dual processes and eight-GPU execution. Existing sampling settings and prompts remain unchanged. v3 also removes the 'open-sourced soon' statement while retaining the same code link; the PDFs alone do not establish actual code availability.

R1.justification: The same 53 cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Related Work moves from Appendix A to Section 2; reference renumbering and expanded author names do not change the literature coverage.

P1.justification: Related Work moves into the main text, and appendices B–D become A–C. There are limited rewrites to contributions and limitations, expanded affiliation text and new experimental subsections, but most existing prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 substantially redesigns the document with recurring laboratory branding, running headers, blue headings, a shaded abstract box, wider text blocks and revised caption/table styling. Existing figures and tables are resized and redistributed, and Table 6 is added. All five scientific figure images retain identical content.

improvement.justification: v1's central adaptive-efficiency claim lacked direct classifier-removal tests and substantive runtime measurements. v3 addresses both gaps: Table 6 and fixed-routing ablations test the router's contribution, while Section 4.3 measures construction, inference and scaling costs with hardware specified. These additions substantially strengthen evidence for the central contribution while preserving earlier results. Missing uncertainty estimates and limited timing-methodology detail still constrain the conclusions.
